title: Token fairshare and stream minimums experiment with contract QA integration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Evaluate a fairshare-style token pricing model and streaming minimums while simultaneously validating contract / security questionnaire (SQ) language and operational controls for enterprise customers. This ticket coordinates the experiment design, telemetry, legal SOW/contract language, and a staged roll-out for hosted API customers.

Hypothesis: Introducing a modest output-weighted price and a transparent per-session streaming minimum (with a fairshare pooling option for enterprise commitments) will improve margin on chat-heavy workloads by at least 12% without materially increasing churn when accompanied by clear docs and contract language. Integrating SQ answers up-front reduces legal friction for enterprise pilots and accelerates revenue capture for early adopters.

Scope: pricing rule experiment (three cohorts), telemetry dashboarding, docs/FAQ, sample contract clauses for SQ answers (KMS, audit logs, retention, on-prem references), sales enablement materials, and a small enterprise pilot with negotiated commit credits.

Non-goal: This ticket does not include changes to SDK client billing meters or major infra re-architecture; those depend on ENG-45390 and will be tracked separately.
experiment_design:
Cohorts:
  - Cohort A (control): current symmetric per-token pricing, no streaming minimums.
  - Cohort B (output-weighted): input tokens charged at 0.7x baseline rate, output tokens charged at 1.3x baseline rate; streaming sessions have a 300-token soft minimum with automatic grace credits for first 3 sessions/month.
  - Cohort C (enterprise fairshare): customers with >$20k/mo commit can opt into a fairshare pool (pooled minimums across sessions) and receive smoothing credits; pricing buckets exposed in contract annex.

Size & sampling: Start internal (redwood-internal API keys), then 2% randomized traffic for public opt-in, then invite 8 enterprise accounts for cohort C pilot.

Duration: 8 weeks measurement window per cohort after stabilization (target rollout start 2026-03-22).

Success metrics:
  - Primary: change in shipped gross margin per token (target +12% for B, +18% for C).
  - Secondary: net new signups attributable to pricing page CTA, retention delta at 30/60 days, support tickets volume change, rate of contract SQ blockers reduced by 50% for pilot customers.

Telemetry: new dashboards in Console (pricing-experiments/fairshare) + Looker queries for unit economics, per-route cost breakdown, and cohort retention. Dashboards linked below.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Telemetry dashboards showing per-cohort unit economics and retention.
2) Contract annex language drafted and pre-cleared by Legal for pilot (SQ redlines done).
3) Implementation roadmap shared with Eng + rollout guardrails defined.
4) Sales enablement one-pager and sample SOW completed.
5) Pilot enterprise accounts enrolled and legal sign-off obtained.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Customer confusion over asymmetric rates. Mitigation: clear billing examples, real-time preflight estimator in pricing calculator, and explicit invoices showing input vs output token breakdown.
Risk: Increased complexity for usage forecasting. Mitigation: provide predicted spend curves and guardrails in Console.
Risk: Legal pushback on minimums or data residency clauses. Mitigation: create contract annex templates and allow per-customer opt-outs into current model during pilot.

decision_points:
1) Whether to make streaming minimums soft (credits/grace) versus hard minimums tied to billing cycles.
2) Precise multipliers for input vs output rates (current proposal 0.7/1.3) vs alternate 0.8/1.2.
3) Contract language for fairshare pool termination and reconciliations.
notes:
- Keep customer-facing messaging focused on 'predictable per-session costs with smoothing for enterprise' rather than 'output surcharge'.
- Coordinate with Dedicated team for cases where enterprise wants private deployment guarantees; ensure SQ answers reference private options.
- Track legal objections during pilot and convert commonly requested changes into an FAQ update.
